title: S3 Access Log Anonymous Requests

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for SI-4 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:s3:accesslogs` events with `operation=REST.GET.OBJECT AND http_status=200` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.154 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:s3:accesslogs` traffic without `operation=REST.GET.OBJECT AND http_status=200`. Confirm UC-4.1.154 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:s3:accesslogs` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

index=aws sourcetype="aws:s3:accesslogs" operation=REST.GET.OBJECT AND http_status=200

description: UC-4.1.154 — S3 Access Log Anonymous Requests: queries AWS `aws:s3:accesslogs` for search criteria `operation=REST.GET.OBJECT AND http_status=200` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On AWS, detecting 'S3 Access Log Anonymous Requests' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.1.154 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable s3 integration in AWS and forward findings/logs via `Splunk_TA_aws` into `index=aws` with `sourcetype=aws:s3:accesslogs`. Validate field extractions before alerting.
visualization: Notable-style table, severity timeline, single-value open finding count.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876) with the modular input for `aws:s3:accesslogs`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `bucket` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable s3 integration in AWS and forward findings/logs via `Splunk_TA_aws` into `index=aws` with `sourcetype=aws:s3:accesslogs`. Validate field extractions before alerting.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:s3:accesslogs" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:s3:accesslogs" operation=REST.GET.OBJECT AND http_status=200
| table _time bucket requester_operation key clientIP
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.154_s3_access_log_anonymous_154"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:s3:accesslogs` in `index=aws` to detect s3 access log anonymous requests. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon S3 console Server access logging for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `bucket` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_154_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Notable-style table, severity timeline, single-value open finding count..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of s3 access log anonymous requests so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
